name: country-code-top-level-domains

description.en: The country-code top-level domain (ccTLD) of each of the 193 UN member states: 193 cards with the country on the front, in English and Swedish, and its two-letter Internet domain on the back, such as Sweden → .se, studied in both directions. Each card gives the domain IANA has delegated to the country's registry, formed from its ISO 3166-1 code except for the United Kingdom (.uk, not .gb); internationalised domains in other scripts and the domains of territories that are not UN members are left out. Compiled from Wikidata and checked against IANA's Root Zone Database and the DNS root zone file.
description.sv: Den nationella toppdomänen (ccTLD) för vart och ett av FN:s 193 medlemsländer: 193 kort med landet på framsidan, på engelska och svenska, och dess tvåbokstaviga internetdomän på baksidan, till exempel Sverige → .se, att öva i båda riktningarna. Varje kort ger den domän som IANA har delegerat till landets domänregister, bildad av landets ISO 3166-1-kod utom för Storbritannien (.uk, inte .gb); internationaliserade domäner i andra skriftsystem och domäner för territorier som inte är medlemmar i FN ingår inte. Sammanställd från Wikidata och kontrollerad mot IANA:s rotzonsdatabas (Root Zone Database) och DNS-rotzonfilen.

method: The research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks against live Wikidata, against downloaded copies of IANA's Root Zone Database and the DNS root zone file, and against the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators; independent AI reviewers may add quality-control rounds after round 0. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.

Selection: the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint was asked for every item that is a member (P463) of the United Nations (Q1065) with no end time on that statement, with its ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (P297) and every top-level Internet domain (P78) statement (query 1, run 2026-10-04). It returned 203 items, 11 of them without an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. As in the library's world-currencies deck, ten of these are historical predecessor states still tagged as members (Islamic State of Afghanistan, Republic of Afghanistan, Kingdom of Laos, Kingdom of Nepal, Mongolian People's Republic, People's Republic of Mozambique, Republic of the Congo (Léopoldville), Somali Democratic Republic, Third Hellenic Republic, realm of the United Kingdom); they were dropped. The eleventh is the Kingdom of Denmark (Q756617), a member without P297; it and the Kingdom of the Netherlands (Q29999, which has P297 "NL") are the recorded members; the cards use Denmark (Q35) and the Netherlands (Q55), whose domains .dk and .nl are also the Kingdoms' P78 values. The resulting 193 items are exactly those of the world-currencies deck, and they were matched one to one with the 193 names on the UN's Member States page downloaded the same day (by normalised English name, the rest through a hand-written table of 28 UN name forms, listed in full under queries, such as "Viet Nam", "Türkiye", "Naoero").

Domains: query 2 asked, for the 193 items and the two Kingdoms, for P297 and every P78 statement with its rank, start and end time, the domain item's English, Swedish and multilingual labels and its classes (P31). For 166 states P78 has exactly one value; for 27 it has more: internationalised (non-Latin) ccTLDs such as .рф, .中国 or .бг (classed Q843214), generic or geographic TLDs such as .quebec, .paris, .swiss, .gov and .mil, the legacy .su for Russia and .gb for the United Kingdom, overseas .wf, .re, .yt and .pm for France, and .eu (deprecated rank) for Belgium and Lithuania. The card's domain is the P78 value of best rank whose label is a dot followed by the state's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in lower case; it is a country code top-level domain (P31 Q42032) for every state. The one exception to the ISO rule is the United Kingdom: its code is GB, but its P78 value of preferred rank is .uk (Q37913), and .gb (Q433862, normal rank) is described as "reserved"; the card gives .uk and a back note explains .gb. The Netherlands item Q55 has no P297 of normal or preferred rank (its "NL" statement is deprecated, so the truthy wdt:P297 of query 2 does not return it); the Kingdom's code NL (Q29999) was used.

Cross-check against IANA: the Root Zone Database table (https://www.iana.org/domains/root/db) was downloaded and parsed into its 1595 rows (316 of type country-code), and the delegation record of each card's domain was fetched (fetch_iana_pages.py, one request per second). Every card's domain is listed with type country-code and a named manager (none is "Not assigned" or "Reserved Domain - IANA"); each card's evidence quotes the row (manager), the record's heading, registration date and last update. Then the root zone file itself (https://www.internic.net/domain/root.zone, SOA serial 2026100301) was downloaded and its NS records counted: every card's domain has NS records, i.e. is delegated in the DNS today.

English and Swedish names of the states: the fronts are those of the library's world-currencies deck, which were reviewed for language there: the Wikidata English and Swedish labels, except China (English label is the long form "People's Republic of China"; the front is the short name "China") and Eswatini (the Swedish label is still "Swaziland"; the Swedish alias "Eswatini" is used). The English fronts are Wikidata's common English short names, so some differ from UN usage (Czech Republic for Czechia, Ivory Coast for Côte d'Ivoire, Cape Verde for Cabo Verde, Turkey for Türkiye); the Swedish fronts are the established Swedish names (Sverige, Storbritannien, USA, Kongo-Kinshasa, Elfenbenskusten, Östtimor …). Every front text is checked against live Wikidata as a label or alias by the builder, except the English "China".

Backs: the domain written as it is conventionally cited, a dot followed by the two lower-case letters (".se"), which is also the English label of the Wikidata domain item. A domain name is text in no language, so the back is tagged zxx. All 193 backs are different, so the deck is studied in both directions.

Back notes, in the compiler's own words, only where a learner would otherwise be misled: the United Kingdom (ISO code GB, domain .uk, .gb reserved: IANA's .gb record names "Reserved Domain - IANA" as manager, Wikidata describes Q433862 as "reserved Internet country-code top level domain for the United Kingdom"); Russia (the Cyrillic .рф and the Soviet Union's .su, both listed by IANA as country-code domains, .рф managed by the Coordination Center for TLD RU and .su by ROSNIIROS, whose address in the .su record is in Moscow, both delegated in the root zone; Wikidata gives .su the country Soviet Union and .рф the country Russia); Timor-Leste (.tl delegated on 23 March 2005; the former .tp of Portuguese Timor, delegated 1997, was later removed: IANA's .tp record says "This domain is not present in the root zone at this time", and its report of 26 January 2015 gives the history; Wikidata gives .tp replaced by .tl). The Swedish notes were written by the compiler.

Machine checks: every card carries Wikidata checks that the builder runs against live Wikidata: the state's English and Swedish label or alias (the front), its P297 code, that its P78 includes the card's domain item, that this item's English label is the card's back and that it is an instance of country code top-level domain (Q42032); and for the notes the labels and countries of .gb, .su and .рф and .tp's replacement by .tl. Every card's evidence quotes Wikidata, IANA's Root Zone Database, the root zone file and the UN page for that state, generated from the downloaded files by gen.py.

Helper scripts (Python 3, standard library, run in a scratch directory; their logic in full): make_q2.py wrote query 2's VALUES list from the country items of the world-currencies dossier's P38 checks plus Q29999 and Q756617. parse_iana.py read the IANA table page and kept every <tr> with exactly three <td> cells as (domain, type, manager, link), text with tags stripped and HTML entities decoded: 1595 rows, 316 with type "country-code". fetch_iana_pages.py fetched https://www.iana.org/domains/root/db/<xx>.html for each card's domain and .gb, .su, .tp (one per second), and took from the <main> text the "Delegation Record for …" heading, the "ccTLD Manager" block, "Registration date" and "Record last updated". rootzone.py split each line of root.zone on whitespace and counted, per owner name (lower case, final dot removed), the lines whose 4th field is NS; the SOA serial is the 7th field of the line owned by "." with type SOA. match_un.py took the text of every <h2> on the UN page after the first (the search heading), 193 names, and matched each to a card by the hand-written table or else by the English front with accents removed and everything but a–z dropped, lower case. gen.py wrote each card from these files: the front from the world-currencies dossier, the back from the best-rank P78 value whose English label is "." plus the ISO code, the Wikidata checks, and the evidence entries (Wikidata statements, the IANA row and record fields, the NS count with the first NS line, and the UN name); it stops if any card's domain is not of type country-code, has a manager "Not assigned" or "Reserved…", or has no NS records, and asserts that the 193 backs are distinct. The notes were written by hand.

Excluded: territories and states that are not UN members, even where IANA lists a country-code domain for them (e.g. .tw, .va, .ps, .gl, .fo, .aw, .aq, .io; Kosovo has no domain in IANA's database); the European Union's .eu, a country-code entry in IANA's database but not a state's; internationalised ccTLDs in other scripts (e.g. .рф, .中国), named only in the Russia note; generic and sponsored TLDs (.gov, .mil, .quebec, .рус …); and retired or legacy domains (.tp, and the Soviet Union's .su), named only in the Timor-Leste and Russia notes.
selection: All 193 member states of the United Nations, one card each, as recorded in Wikidata (member of Q1065 with no end time, less ten historical predecessor items, none of which has an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code) and confirmed against the UN's Member States page on 2026-10-04; the Kingdoms of Denmark (Q756617, no ISO code in Wikidata) and the Netherlands (Q29999) are represented by Denmark (Q35) and the Netherlands (Q55). Each card gives the country-code top-level domain for the state's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code that IANA has delegated to the country's registry, as recorded in Wikidata (P78) and confirmed by IANA's Root Zone Database and the root zone file of 2026-10-04; the United Kingdom, whose ISO code is GB, gets .uk, its delegated domain, with a note on the reserved .gb. Left out: territories and non-member states (Taiwan, the Holy See, Palestine, Kosovo, dependencies such as Greenland or Aruba), internationalised ccTLDs in non-Latin scripts, the European Union's .eu, generic and sponsored TLDs such as .gov or .quebec, and retired or legacy domains; Russia's .рф and .su and Timor-Leste's former .tp are mentioned in back notes only.
licensing: The deck is CC0 1.0. Its only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of states, each state's domain and the English and Swedish names come from it (China's English short name and the notes are the compiler's own wording of facts). IANA's Root Zone Database and the root zone file (ICANN terms of service: no licence to reproduce; IANA's CC0 statement covers only its protocol registries, not the root zone database) and the UN Member States page (personal non-commercial use only) were used only to verify facts that Wikidata gave: no list, selection or running text was copied from them, and the selection of states follows Wikidata, not their lists. The evidence in the provenance report quotes each of them briefly, one entry at a time, as citations for verification; read as a whole, the evidence column thus cites the UN's name for every state and IANA's manager and dates for every domain. These are factual names and dates given as citations, and the cards themselves contain none of them except the domain name itself. Which domain is delegated for a country is a fact and not protected by copyright, so verifying it against these sources puts no conditions on the deck.

rounds.lens: Machine and source checks: every card's domain compared across Wikidata (P78 and P297), IANA's Root Zone Database (table and delegation record) and the root zone file; the selection compared with the UN Member States page; Wikidata checks run by the builder.
rounds.summary: For all 193 states Wikidata's best-rank P78 includes the ASCII ccTLD formed from the state's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (for the United Kingdom .uk, see below), IANA lists that domain as a country-code TLD with a manager, and the root zone of 2026-10-04 delegates it (NS records). No card's domain disagrees between the sources. The UN page lists the same 193 states. The builder's 1166 Wikidata checks (581 on labels: every front label, and each domain item's label; the others on P297, P78, the domain item's class and the note facts) pass against live Wikidata. The findings below record where Wikidata holds further or unexpected values and how the cards deal with them.

findings.issue: The United Kingdom's ISO 3166-1 code is GB, but its domain in use is .uk. Wikidata's P78 has .uk (preferred) and .gb (normal rank); IANA lists .gb with manager "Reserved Domain - IANA", and it still has NS records in the root zone.
findings.resolution: The card gives .uk, the domain IANA delegates to a registry (Nominet UK); the back note says the ISO code is GB and that .gb exists but IANA lists it as reserved (wording revised in round 1). The note does not claim .gb is undelegated, since the root zone still has NS records for it.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P78 for Russia has four values of equal (normal) rank: .ru, .su, .рф and .рус (the last a generic TLD).
findings.resolution: The card gives .ru, the domain for Russia's ISO code RU; the note names .рф and the Soviet-era .su (both country-code domains in IANA's database, both delegated). .рус, a generic TLD in IANA's database, is not mentioned.

findings.issue: Timor-Leste's domain changed: the former .tp is still a country-code entry in IANA's database but is "not present in the root zone".
findings.resolution: The card gives .tl; the back note says it was delegated in 2005 and replaced .tp, since removed (IANA record and its 2015 report; Wikidata .tp replaced by .tl).

findings.issue: The Netherlands item Q55 has no P297 of normal or preferred rank in Wikidata (its "NL" statement is deprecated, which the truthy wdt:P297 path of query 2 does not return; corrected in round 3); the Kingdom of the Netherlands (Q29999), the UN member, has P297 "NL" and P78 .nl.
findings.resolution: The card uses Q55 for the names (as in the world-currencies deck) and checks NL and .nl on Q29999 as well as .nl on Q55.

findings.issue: Wikidata's English label of Q148 is the long form "People's Republic of China".
findings.resolution: Front "China", as in the world-currencies deck; no English label check for it.

findings.issue: Wikidata lists .eu as a P78 value of Belgium and Lithuania (deprecated rank); .eu is the European Union's domain, not a country's.
findings.resolution: Ignored, as deprecated values are; the cards give .be and .lt.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P78 for France includes the overseas domains .wf, .re, .yt and .pm and the geographic TLDs .paris, .bzh and .alsace (normal rank) beside .fr (preferred rank).
findings.resolution: The card gives .fr, the domain for France's ISO code FR; the territories' domains belong to their own ISO codes and are left out with the non-member territories.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P78 for Saudi Arabia includes an internationalised ccTLD item (Q137014) whose English label is the transliteration "AlSaudiah" rather than the domain.
findings.resolution: Not used: internationalised ccTLDs are excluded from every card; the card gives .sa.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P78 for the United States includes .gov and .mil (normal rank) beside .us (preferred rank).
findings.resolution: The card gives .us, the country-code domain for the ISO code US; .gov and .mil are of type "sponsored" in IANA's database and are left out. No note added, to keep the card to one fact.

rounds.scope: All 193 cards: codes against iso-codes (pycountry), delegation against the live root zone, membership against the UN page, the three back notes against IANA records; builder checks re-run.
rounds.summary: No factual errors found. One suggestion on the United Kingdom note and the description's wording, verified and applied.

findings.issue: The note "IANA lists .gb as a reserved domain" could be read as .gb not being in the DNS, but .gb is still delegated (3 NS records in the root zone; IANA's record names Jisc as contact). The description's "the domain IANA has delegated for the country" is imprecise, since .gb is delegated too.
findings.resolution: Verified: root.zone (SOA 2026100301) has 3 NS records for gb. (ns.uu.net., ns0.ja.net., ns4.ja.net.) and IANA's .gb record names Jisc as contact. Note reworded to "… its domain is .uk; .gb also exists, but IANA lists it as reserved." (sv likewise); the suggested "not open for registration" was not used, as none of the deck's sources states it. Evidence for .gb's NS records and contact added. Description and selection now say "the domain IANA has delegated to the country's registry".
